idea: a rounded card pairing one icon with a short label, naming a single item among peers
outline: solid surface backing rect (crisp) so nothing drawn beneath shows through
sketched rounded outline, stroke token carrying valence
icon (plain or in a disc), left of or above the label
one or two line label, vertically centred in the remaining space
variation_seen: orientation: icon-left row (b16, b23, b28) versus icon-top tile (b19, b20)
icon treatment: plain kit.icon (b16, b19) versus Loom.th.iconDisc (b20, b23, b28)
valence on the frame: muted thin versus accent4 thick (b16), neg stroke (b19), default ink elsewhere
label lines 1 or 2, role lead/label/body, sizes 30 to 40
extras riding on the card: a cross mark (b19), an owner chip row (b28)
but b20, b23 and b28 are the same three conditions (same icons, near-same words) re-drawn in three layouts, so the real distinct uses are about three, all in one lesson and one style

future_uses.shows: red-flag cards: mail icon 'unknown sender', link icon 'mismatched URL', clock icon 'urgent deadline'
feature tiles: one icon plus the feature name per card in a row of three or four
risk factor cards that later receive a tick or an owner, like the conditions here
process step cards along a flow, each with a step icon and a two-word label

slots_sketch: icon (a caller may draw a custom glyph or a peep instead)
reason: The idea is genuinely topic-independent, but the five uses are one lesson in one style and three of them are the same three conditions re-drawn, so the evidence is about three distinct uses with a two-layout, two-icon-style spread that no lesson has yet shown it wants to share. Each copy is three or four kit calls, so a component saves little today; the one recurring fix (a crisp solid backing under a sketched outline) is worth capturing once a second or third lesson confirms which layout and icon treatment actually recur.
